country.title: Bangladesh on the map
country.text: Bangladesh is in South Asia, at the top of the Bay of Bengal. India surrounds it on the west, north and east, and Myanmar touches the south-east corner. Most of the country is a flat, green delta built by three great rivers: the Padma, the Jamuna and the Meghna. Tap a division to lift it out of the map.
facts: Location: 20°34′ to 26°38′ North, 88°01′ to 92°41′ East
Area: about 148,000 square kilometres
8 divisions, 64 districts and 495 upazilas
Rivers: 1,415 on the official list published in 2025
Neighbours: India and Myanmar. Sea: Bay of Bengal
The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of the country
Capital: Dhaka. Time zone: UTC+6
People: about 170 million (2022 census)
Credit: the map artwork is from our team. Division borders are from geoBoundaries (CC BY 4.0)

divisions.name: Khulna
divisions.tag: Home of the Sundarbans and the tiger
divisions.text: Khulna is the south-west corner of Bangladesh, where the land meets the mangrove forest. The Sundarbans, home of the Royal Bengal Tiger, is here. So is Bagerhat with its Sixty Dome Mosque. The division is also known for shrimp farming and the sea port of Mongla.
facts: Famous for: the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest on Earth
The Sixty Dome Mosque in Bagerhat, a UNESCO World Heritage site
Kushtia, home of the mystic singer Lalon and of Tagore's house at Shilaidaha
Mongla sea port and the shrimp called white gold

divisions.name: Rajshahi
divisions.text: Rajshahi lies along the Padma River in the north-west. It is the land of mangoes and fine silk. It also holds some of the oldest sites in the country, from the great Buddhist monastery of Paharpur to the ruined city of Mahasthangarh and the Sultanate mosques of Gaur.
facts: Famous for: Paharpur (Somapura Mahavihara), a UNESCO World Heritage site
Mahasthangarh in Bogura, the oldest known city in Bangladesh
Mangoes of Chapainawabganj and Rajshahi silk
Chhota Sona, Bagha and Kusumba mosques, and the sweet yoghurt of Bogura

divisions.name: Rangpur
divisions.text: Rangpur is the far north of Bangladesh, a wide farming plain fed by the Teesta River. On a clear winter morning you can see the snow peak of Kanchenjunga from Tetulia. The division is known for the terracotta Kantajew Temple, Tajhat Palace and the litchis of Dinajpur.
facts: Famous for: Kantajew Temple in Dinajpur, covered in terracotta
Tetulia in Panchagarh, the northern tip of the country
Tajhat Palace and the Teesta Barrage
Birthplace of Begum Rokeya, pioneer of women's education

divisions.name: Barishal
divisions.text: Barishal is a land of rivers and canals, where boats are as common as cars. It has long been called the granary of Bengal for its rice. Floating markets sell guava and vegetables from boats, and at Kuakata beach you can watch both the sunrise and the sunset over the sea.
facts: Famous for: Kuakata, the daughter of the sea
Floating guava markets of Jhalokathi and Pirojpur
Hilsa fish and the big river launches to Dhaka
Bhola, the largest island of Bangladesh

divisions.name: Sylhet
divisions.text: Sylhet is the green north-east, known for rolling tea gardens and heavy rain. Clear rivers come down from the Meghalaya hills at Jaflong, Bichanakandi and Lalakhal. In the monsoon, huge wetlands called haors turn into inland seas. Many pilgrims visit the shrine of Hazrat Shah Jalal.
facts: Famous for: the tea estates of Sreemangal, the tea capital
Ratargul Swamp Forest and Tanguar Haor
Jaflong, Bichanakandi and Lalakhal
Shrines of Hazrat Shah Jalal and Shah Paran, and seven-layer tea

divisions.name: Chattogram
divisions.tag: Sea, hills and the main port
divisions.text: Chattogram is the largest division and the gateway to the sea. Its port handles most of the country's trade. To the south is Cox's Bazar beach, and to the east rise the green Hill Tracts of Rangamati, Bandarban and Khagrachhari, home to many indigenous communities.
facts: Famous for: Cox's Bazar, one of the longest natural sea beaches in the world
Saint Martin's, the only coral island of Bangladesh
Kaptai Lake, Sajek Valley and the highest peaks of the country
Mezban feast of Chattogram and the rosmalai of Cumilla

divisions.name: Dhaka
divisions.tag: The capital and the heart of the country
divisions.text: Dhaka Division holds the capital city, one of the busiest and most crowded cities on Earth. Old Dhaka still has Mughal forts, the Pink Palace and streets full of biryani shops. The division is also the centre of government, business and the garment industry.
facts: Famous for: Lalbagh Fort, Ahsan Manzil and the National Parliament building by Louis Kahn
Sonargaon, the old capital of Bengal, and the home of jamdani weaving
The Padma Bridge links Dhaka to the south-west
Known as the city of mosques and the rickshaw capital of the world

divisions.name: Mymensingh
divisions.text: Mymensingh became the eighth division in 2015. It sits on the old Brahmaputra River, below the Garo Hills. The city is a centre of education and folk culture, and the home of the Zainul Abedin art museum. The region gave Bengal the folk ballads called Mymensingh Gitika.
facts: Famous for: Bangladesh Agricultural University
Zainul Abedin Museum by the Brahmaputra
China clay hills of Birishiri in Netrokona and the Garo Hills
The monda sweet of Muktagacha

places.name: Dhaka
places.text: Dhaka is the capital and the biggest city of Bangladesh, on the Buriganga river. Old Dhaka has Lalbagh Fort and Ahsan Manzil, and the new city has the National Parliament by Louis Kahn.

places.name: Gopalganj
places.text: Gopalganj is in the south of Dhaka Division, on the Madhumati river.

places.name: Mymensingh
places.text: Mymensingh stands on the old Brahmaputra river and is home to the Agricultural University and the Shilpacharya Zainul Abedin museum.

places.name: Bogura
places.text: Bogura is home to Mahasthangarh, the oldest city site found in Bangladesh, and to its famous yoghurt.

places.name: Naogaon
places.text: Naogaon is home to the Paharpur Buddhist Vihara, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Rajshahi
places.text: Rajshahi sits on the Padma river and is famous for silk and mangoes.

places.name: Panchagarh
places.text: Panchagarh is the northern tip of the country. On clear days you can see Kanchenjunga from Tetulia.

places.name: Rangpur
places.text: Rangpur is the main city of the north, known for Tajhat Palace and Begum Rokeya.

places.name: Barishal
places.text: Barishal is a city of rivers and canals, often called the Venice of Bengal.

places.name: Patuakhali
places.text: Patuakhali has Kuakata, where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the sea.

places.name: Bandarban
places.text: Bandarban is a hill district with Nilgiri, Boga Lake and the Nafakhum waterfall.

places.name: Chattogram
places.text: Chattogram is the second city of Bangladesh and its main sea port, between green hills and the Bay of Bengal.

places.name: Cumilla
places.text: Cumilla has the Mainamati Buddhist ruins and is famous for its rasmalai.

places.name: Cox's Bazar
places.text: Cox’s Bazar has the longest natural sea beach in the world, about 120 km of unbroken sand.

places.name: Rangamati
places.text: Rangamati sits on the blue Kaptai Lake, with its hanging bridge and hill villages.

places.name: Maulvibazar
places.text: Maulvibazar holds Sreemangal, the tea capital of Bangladesh.

places.name: Sunamganj
places.text: Sunamganj is the land of haors, with Tanguar Haor, a huge seasonal wetland.

places.name: Sylhet
places.text: Sylhet is the city of tea gardens, hills and the shrine of Hazrat Shah Jalal.

places.name: Bagerhat
places.text: Bagerhat is the mosque city of Khan Jahan Ali, home of the Sixty Dome Mosque.

places.name: Khulna
places.text: Khulna is the gateway to the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world.

places.name: Sundarbans
places.text: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world and the home of the Royal Bengal Tiger. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Sreemangal
places.text: Sreemangal is the tea capital of Bangladesh, with green tea gardens as far as you can see.

places.name: Jaflong
places.text: Jaflong is a river valley at the foot of the Meghalaya hills, with clear water and stones.

places.name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
places.text: Ratargul is a freshwater swamp forest. In the monsoon you go through it by boat.

places.name: Bichanakandi
places.text: Bichanakandi is a stony river bed where streams come down from the hills.

places.name: Lalakhal
places.text: Lalakhal is a river famous for its blue-green water.

places.name: Tanguar Haor
places.text: Tanguar Haor is a huge seasonal wetland, full of birds and fish.

places.name: Sajek Valley
places.text: Sajek Valley sits high in the Rangamati hills, often above a sea of clouds.

places.name: Saint Martin’s Island
places.alias: saint martin|st martin|st. martin|saint martins|st martins|narikel jinjira
places.text: Saint Martin’s is the only coral island of Bangladesh, at the south end of the country.

places.name: Kuakata
places.text: Kuakata is a long beach where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the sea.

places.name: Paharpur
places.text: Paharpur has the ruins of Somapura Mahavihara, a great Buddhist monastery and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Mahasthangarh
places.text: Mahasthangarh is the oldest city site found in Bangladesh, more than 2,000 years old.

places.name: Sonargaon
places.text: Sonargaon was the old capital of Bengal. Panam City and the folk art museum are here.

places.name: Savar
places.text: Savar is home to the National Martyrs’ Memorial.

places.name: Tetulia
places.text: From Tetulia, on clear days, you can see the snowy peak of Kanchenjunga.

places.name: Kaptai Lake
places.text: Kaptai Lake is the biggest man-made lake in Bangladesh, in the Rangamati hills.

places.name: Nafakhum
places.text: Nafakhum is one of the widest waterfalls in Bangladesh, deep in the Bandarban hills.
